newsitem.title: UK: Enron, CATS wait judgement despite J-Block settlem.
newsitem.headline: Enron, CATS wait judgement despite J-Block settlem.

text.p: The judgement expected in the High Court on Tuesday in a dispute between Enron Corp and the owners of the North Sea's Central Area Transmission System (CATS) will go ahead regardless of Monday's settlement between Enron and partners in the North Sea's J-Block, a spokesman for CATS said on Monday.
The J-Block producers said in a statement that the judgement will not impact on the J-Block settlement.

Enron as purchaser of J-Block gas and BG Exploration and Production, Agip (UK) Ltd and Phillips Petroleum Company United Kingdom Ltd, as producers, announced on Monday that they had settled J-Block litigation and Enron would pay $440 million in cash to the producers.

A spokesman for Amoco, owner of 29.5289 percent of CATS, said after the J-Block announcement that it was an entirely separate issue from the CATS dispute, and that Amoco and CATS were still awaiting the court's judgement.

He said that the CATS partners initiated legal action by filing a writ against Teesside Gas Transportation Ltd (TGTL), an Enron subsidiary, in March 1995. He added that the CATS members and TGTL had signed a Capacity Reservation and Transportation Agreement (CRTA) in 1990, which took effect in April 1993.

Under the CRTA, TGTL had leased capacity in CATS and started to pay for it from April 1993. But the spokesman for Amoco said that TGTL stopped paying in October 1994, which was why CATS then filed a writ the following spring.
Enron in turn filed a counter claim, he said, alleging that CATS was unable to provide the transportation services contracted for.
Both the CATS claim and the Enron counterclaim are being heard together, and judgement is due on Tuesday.

As well as Amoco, CATS is owned by Amerada Hess Ltd (17.7174 percent), British Gas Exploration and Production Ltd (39.3719 percent), BG North Sea Holdings Ltd (11.8116 percent), Phillips Petroleum Co (UK) Ltd (0.663 percent), Fina Exploration Ltd (0.5684 percent) and Agip (UK) Ltd (0.3388 percent).
